quest.title: Dream of Awakening
quest.description: One day, you and Paimon notice that many people in Sumeru City are talking about dreams...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x575, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Hello, Traveler. Have you ever heard of "A Moment of Dreams"?

choices.text: "A Moment of Dreams"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that sounds like some kind of sweet drink!

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: Haha, I'm afraid not. It's the name of an event we started to hold regularly.

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: Dreams have become quite the hot topic in Sumeru, and many people are excited to share the dreams they've seen at night.

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: The same goes for me! The last time I dreamed was when I was but a little child, so I can't help but feel excited and nostalgic about dreaming again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right, everyone's able to dream again now!

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: Yes! We organized an event to give everyone with new dreams a platform to freely share their experiences.

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: And thus our event, "A Moment of Dreams," was born.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So it's kinda like a fireside chat...

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: You could say that. We hear all sorts of wild and fabulous stories every day. Really, why not have a listen for yourselves?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I can understand your curiosity...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, but to us, dreaming is as normal as breathing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but if there are free drinks and snacks involved, then Paimon might consider it!

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: Oh really? So you mean... you've already seen many dreams?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm-hmm, but no need to get so excited, it's really nothing special.

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: No no no, we need experienced participants like you to share your experiences with dreaming.

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: Please allow me to address you two as "dream experts"!

choices.text: ...Sounds kinda weird.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, "expert." Hehe, Paimon kinda likes it!

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: Now you seem interested, hehe. Please, follow me to the meeting place. It won't take much of your time.

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: Rest assured, you'll find all the drinks and snacks you'd like there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, how accommodating!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sign us up! Ah, but wait... Paimon's getting ahead of herself again. We should see what the Traveler thinks first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Why aren't you saying anything?

choices.text: You're the boss...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe! Alright, hurry up and take us to be dream experts!

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: Haha, very good. Follow me, then.

choices.text: I don't think I really have a choice.
There are some things that "expert" just doesn't seem to go with...
What's that?

talks.objective: Follow Pedrush to "A Moment of Dreams"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, their questions were way too difficult. We don't actually know anything more than they do. We're just more experienced dreamers, that's all.

choices.text: They didn't really care about the answers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You do have a point. It's more rewarding to explore and contemplate the meaning of a question than to focus on the answer itself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right now, these people are like wanderers who've starved for three days and three nights and are desperate to replenish their energy. Any explanation they get now is like pure sustenance to them, no matter how good the explanation really is!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and now that Paimon has said that, you know who comes to mind?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Nahida.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bingo! If she was here, she'd probably be making some similar analogy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Unfortunately, she's super busy right now, and may not have time for gatherings like this.

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: Dear experts, we have another guest who would like to consult you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? But you saw how we answered all the questions just now... We're not really all that knowledgeable.

response.speaker: Pedrush
response.text: Ah, but this guest is rather... special.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: My question is, why didn't you immediately tell me about such an interesting place?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, Nahida!? How did you get here!?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Interesting events like "A Moment of Dreams" don't happen every day, after all. No matter how busy things are, I'd still set aside some time to check it out.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Anyway, I really didn't expect to meet you here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! If there's anyone that understands dreams, it's you! You should be able to help us answer all these questions!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You're not wrong. All right, they can ask me anything. The more interesting, the better.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Huh? What's wrong? You were all so excited a minute ago... why the sudden hesitation?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think they need to build up some courage first.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Even so, it's not like I look super intimidating or anything, right?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: And in terms of reputation and renown, you've also done many great things in Sumeru, yet they didn't even flinch at you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Still, not quite the same as approaching an archon.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Alas, the interesting questions have all vanished in an instant. It appears I'm the one spoiling the fun here. I'll see myself out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, that's not true, Nahida!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I don't want to get in the way of the original purpose of "A Moment of Dreams," which is to let people gather here and freely share their marvelous dreams.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Now the atmosphere here is like water poured into a container... The water is more secure and settled, but it has lost its free-flowing nature from the river.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I just wanted to be another drop in the water, not the cold and restrictive container.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is she doing what I think she is...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's sulking...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, hey, it's all right, everyone. No need to be shy! The Dendro Archon is really nice, so please, just go ahead and ask! Otherwise, she'll leave.

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: A—Alright... I'll give it a try.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it's the slime guy.

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: Hey, drop the nicknames, would ya? Besides... I don't want to become a Slime anymore. Maybe a Finch or fish is more suitable for me.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I see. So you want to become a small animal in your dreams, right? Why do you think that sounds good to you?

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: I guess I just want to experience something different. My everyday life is nothing but the same...

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: The sky is right above me, and the ocean just over the horizon, yet I remain caged in a life of monotony.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So you want to experience something new in your dreams... Sorry, I'm getting a little confused. Why don't you seek out some new experiences in real life?

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: Because if I don't work, I won't have any Mora. Sure, I don't want to be out hammering nails and cutting wood every day, but I have aging parents and young children to take care of.

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: By the time this all dawned on me, I realized that my life has already been filled to the brim by trifling matters, and I have no more freedom.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But if that's the case, then even if you became a flying bird or swimming fish, you will still be hammering nails and cutting wood in your dreams.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The reason is you've already been caged. It doesn't matter what your physical body turns into, your mind will still be stuck in the same predicament.

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: Really? That sounds pretty terrible! Then what should I do?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I don't know everything that you're going through, but how about replacing your hammer?

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: Huh? Replacing my hammer?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That's right. Having worked for such a long time, you of all people must know what makes a good hammer.

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: Well, of course. A good hammer needs to be heavy enough to drive the nail in with just a couple taps... and the handle has to have a good grip to it — not too smooth.

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: Come to think of it, I haven't replaced my current hammer in quite some time.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You should replace it. Then decorate the handle with something you like... maybe some ornaments, fur, or a hard leather wrapping. Then, write the names of your children on it.

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: That makes sense... I think it'd give me a good boost of energy at work!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: A new sense of adventure often begins with the little things in life.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You don't need to become a bird in the air or fish in the sea. You only need to do your best in life, and all those things you cherish will become your source of happiness.

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: Yes, yes... I get it now. This is a real eye-opener for me!

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: I'll go and pick out a new hammer right away... No, I should make one of my own. Thank you, great Dendro Archon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's our Nahida! Only you would know how to get right to the heart of the problem.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Actually, I didn't really understand the problem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I gave him that advice because I once saw a worker doing the same thing. Whenever he became tired, he would look at some names on the handle of his tool.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: After a moment, he'd start to smile. It really surprised me at the time... My guess is that the names on the handle were of important people to him.

choices.text: I think I understand.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Mm-hmm. After observation, I know this kind of behavior motivates people... but why is that?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Is it because of excitement, anticipation, or helplessness? I really don't know... And even if I could know what's going through his mind, it's still difficult to fully grasp his feelings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon gets what you mean... Huh, Paimon had no idea it takes you so much effort to understand these kinds of things...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hehe, that's why I was a bit nervous just now. But luckily, seeing his happy face in the end reassured me that I didn't say anything wrong.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Don't mind me, though. This is just my way of learning.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm happy to help if you ever need it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, don't forget about Paimon! Everyone knows that Paimon's also super skilled at reading people's feelings!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Thanks, you two. That makes me feel a lot better. Let's move on to the next question, shall we?

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I already asked the experts my question earlier, but I wanted to hear the Dendro Archon's response, too.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: What should I do if I want to see my deceased wife in my dreams every night?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm, longing for the deceased...

choices.text: (Is she remembering something about Greater Lord Rukkhadevata?)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Even if you keep reliving those beautiful memories, it'll only highlight the emptiness in your real life.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: If your wife were still alive, she certainly wouldn't want to see you like this, would she?

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: No, I suppose not... But our time together in my dreams is not just reliving our past together.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I don't know. Maybe it's because I miss her too much, but it's really as if she had come back to life in my dreams.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: She even remembers each and every dream. After I wake up and then continue dreaming again later, we can pick up our conversation right where we last left off.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That's really amazing. Statistically speaking, continuous dreams are extremely rare.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: It's almost as if my wife has obtained a second life in my dreams. But the more vivid she appears, the emptier I feel and the more painful it is when I wake up. I don't know whether to call it a blessing or a curse...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Maybe all of this is rooted in your deep longing for her.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Were there any unresolved matters or regrets between the two of you?

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I don't know... I suppose my biggest regret is that I couldn't spend the rest of my life with her.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I really felt like I was ready to move on. I wouldn't be so hesitant now if it weren't for these hyper-realistic dreams I've been having.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. You know, they say that whatever's on your mind is what goes into your dreams.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But dreams are, and will forever be, just dreams. We are people living in the real world.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's not good to be overly obsessed with dreams. All it'll do is fill up your mind and eat away at your thoughts.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Yes, I know... That's why I'm also a little disappointed in myself. I still need to take care of our child.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: And it's probably not good to let her see me in such a state...

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: *sigh* Anyway, thanks for your advice, great Dendro Archon.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hmm, I'm a little worried about him. I hope he can find a way to cheer up soon.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I think I can handle things from here. You don't need to stay here if you find it boring. You're here to have a good time, after all.

choices.text: (No, she shouldn't be able to remember anymore.)
You were just drawing from a similar example.
Vivid dreams are just really exciting to them.

talks.objective: Check on Ilman, who is depressed

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you feeling any better now?

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Yes. I think the Dendro Archon made a really good point. I need to stop dwelling on my wife like this and move on with my life.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Now that I think about it, my wife and I always meet at a familiar place in my dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: I know where that place exists in reality, but it's a bit far and dangerous. I don't dare to go there on my own.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: But, at the same time, I feel as if I should go and have a look anyway. Perhaps I'll be able to move on once I see that there's nothing there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like a good plan.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Otherwise, I'll keep on feeling like everything is covered in a haze... like I'm only half-awake.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Once I can stop dreaming about that place, I'll probably be able to get my life back together.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Actually, you two are adventurers, right? If it's okay with you, could you escort me to that place?

choices.text: Sure, let's go have a look.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it might also be a good chance for us to unwind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even if you can't see your wife there, taking in some nice scenery will definitely help cheer you up.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Yeah, I hope so too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, go ahead and get yourself ready then.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Speaking of longing for the deceased, I'd better tell Nahida about Greater Lord Rukkhadevata.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Nahida should at least know that she once existed in this world.)

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Ahem! Are you headed off to some interesting place without telling me again?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, wait, aren't you supposed to be answering questions?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I just finished. And I really got a lot out of it... so many interesting and novel thoughts.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Anyway, it looks like you're going somewhere. Why don't you take me with you?

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Oh, there's no need to trouble you, great Dendro Archon. I imagine you must have many other important things to deal with.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: No need to stand on ceremony. Besides, I wouldn't have asked to come along if I didn't have a good reason.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I wanted to use this opportunity to discuss with you some things that are puzzling me right now.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Hmm, I didn't know the great Dendro Archon could become puzzled, too...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I'm not all that different from you, you know. All right, let's go. We can talk on the way.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I'd better go with her. The whole Greater Lord Rukkhadevata thing will take some explaining...)

choices.text: Let's go get a breath of fresh air.

talks.objective: Go to the place Ilman mentioned

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back already. How did it go?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We have an emergency on our hands. Please notify everyone here that while they can continue to discuss their dreams, they mustn't try to visit or recreate the locations and scenes that they have been experiencing in them.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: What? A—Alright, if that's the wish of the great Dendro Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: But could you at least tell me what happened? You all look so serious...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Pedrush what happened on your trip with Ilman.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: I see, I never knew even a dream could be so dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Don't worry. I'll be sure to notify all the event participants, and inform the other staff members about what has happened.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Using the event registration list, I should be able to contact more people that were interested in dreams, and warn them about the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Thank you, that would be very helpful.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Let me confirm if all of today's participants are still here...

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Ata has already left... It seemed that he was on his way to make a hammer, so that shouldn't be a problem. Oh? Wait a second... Where's Kathya?

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Has anyone seen Kathya? Has she already left?

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: Oh, I think she already left. She said there was somewhere she wanted to go...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, did she want to look for the place from her dreams, too?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Can you tell us where she went?

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: Yes, she did briefly mention it... somewhere near Chatrakam Cave.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Alright, thank you. We'll go look for her.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Please help us tell the others not to do anything reckless.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: Sure thing. *sigh* Who would have known things would've turned out like this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, it's always nice to go for a leisurely stroll!

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Do adventurers often go to places like this?

choices.text: Yes, of course.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Hmm, I guess so.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So this is where you always meet your wife in your dreams?

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Yes, for the most part. Our place is on the summit just up ahead.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: When I saw her in my dreams, we didn't do anything but talk about ordinary, mundane topics.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I'd tell her about our daughter, Haydar, and she always listened intently.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: She would also reminisce about the past with me, telling me interesting stories and cracking jokes.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: It feels like no matter how long we may chat, it's never enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sometimes, it's the little things in life that matter the most.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: This is the part I'm a little puzzled about...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I am very familiar with dreams, and normally, they lack logic and continuity.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But you said she could remember what you had told her before, right?

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: That's right. She always listened to me carefully in real life, and now, she's doing the same in my dreams.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: She always surprises me with some details from our lives in the real world. The fact that she can remember such things makes me feel like she's alive.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, that's pretty weird... Well, dreams are kinda weird to begin with.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: However, the problem is that his dreams have too much structure and continuity. Most dreams are far more fragile than you could imagine.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: For example, a loud noise outside your window in the real world could cause your dream self to get loaded into and fired out of a big cannon.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Another example... If you're thirsty in the real world, then you might find yourself trudging through a desert in your dream.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But the appearance of your wife seems unusually stable and unaffected by any outside interference. Statistically, this should be extremely rare.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I don't understand it either, but I have no reason to suspect or reject these dreams. They're too beautiful.

choices.text: Indeed.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But I still want to figure out the how and the why. These kinds of dreams are novel to me as well. That's why I want to have a look at the scene your dreams have been taking place at.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Let's go! Just think of it as a nice little hike to the top of the mountain.

choices.text: I agree, it doesn't really feel like a cause for concern.
We usually journey through far more dangerous places than this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, he really wasn't kidding. This place definitely isn't safe.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: No matter. We'll just finish them quickly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you going to fight too, Nahida?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Of course. This is all part of our little trip.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: It's just sleepwalking, they're really overreacting.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: *yawn* I'm getting really sleepy.

talks.objective: Defeat the monsters in front of you

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The scenery here is amazing... It also seems like a great spot for eating snacks and taking a nap.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wouldn't mind spending some time here every day, either. *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I've yet to see anything strange about this place.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I do not plan to deny the power of longing. Such an intense but unquantifiable emotion could indeed have the power to organize dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: His wife must be a really amazing person.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, where'd he go?

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Oh, so you were waiting for me here? Well, guess what, I've brought someone amazing with me today.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: When the Dendro Archon said she wanted to come with me, I could hardly believe it!

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: I'll bring Haydar once I'm more familiar with the way here. She's been telling me that she really misses you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wh—What's wrong with him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's nobody there.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Wait, Maynar. Don't go that way, it's dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, he's gonna fall. Catch him!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew, luckily he didn't fall... But what was all that rambling about? He also looks like he's passed out...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: He's in a dream now. What he said just now matches almost perfectly with the dreams he described to us earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? So... he fell asleep, and started to have the same dream?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I find it a little strange as well, but we mustn't awaken someone while they're sleepwalking. All we can do is sit here and wait.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Uh... Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: Maynar... Where's Maynar?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, good! You're finally awake.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: What happened...

choices.text: You were sleepwalking...

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Huh? Sleepwalking?

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Oh, right... It was all just a dream...

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: The moment I reached the summit, I saw my wife, Maynar, sitting there, and walked over to her.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: After I introduced her to you, she seemed a little flustered and started walking away. I told her to stop because of the cliff...

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: And then she seemed to suddenly disappear. A strong wind started to blow around me and the sky grew dark.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: When I realized something wasn't right, I woke up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds pretty wild... Maybe you were just too tired.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I don't think so... I slept a lot yesterday, and I don't feel very sleepy now.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Maybe we've affected the way his subconscious constructs dreams by following him here.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Anyway, all that matters is that you woke up safe and sound.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: I think I know what happened now, I'm sorry... If it weren't for you, I would have fallen.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Let's head back now. Don't come back to this place again for the time being.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: ...O—Okay.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nahida, what's on your mind? Paimon's a little worried now.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: We still don't have enough evidence to work off of, so it's hard to draw any reliable conclusions yet... But I'm concerned that Ilman's case may not be unique to him...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right, come to think of it, there were lots of people from the event who had vivid memories of their dreams!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe this phenomenon is already spreading.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Right, and not only at "A Moment of Dreams." There may be people like this all across Sumeru.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: We need to understand what's happening and the rate of its development as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then there's no time to lose. Let's head back!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Stop standing there, Ilman! Let's go!

choices.text: And almost fell.

talks.objective: Return to "A Moment of Dreams" to ascertain the situation

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Sorry to interrupt, everyone. We finally have some REAL dream experts joining us!

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Esteemed experts, this way, please. Ahem, now, if anyone has any questions, please feel free to ask them.

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: They must be dream experts from another land... Great!

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: Oh, I have a question! Me first! Me first!

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: No rush. Everyone, please line up and ask in an orderly fashion!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After some initial commotion, everyone finally forms a queue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, Paimon didn't expect them to be so enthusiastic...

dialogues.speaker: Ata
dialogues.text: My question is simple. My everyday life is very difficult, so I would like to become a Slime in my dreams. How can I do that?

choices.text: Oh, that's a tough one...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon knows! Paimon's had this kind of dream before, so she knows a thing or two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The first time, Paimon became an Anemo Slime. Paimon was shot by an adventurer's arrow and flew in the sky all night long.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The second time, Paimon became a Dendro Slime. A group of kids thought Paimon was a Radish and pulled out all the grass on her head. It was super painful!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The third time, Paimon became a Cryo Slime. In the end, Paimon was captured by a chef and turned into a smoothie.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And the fourth time, Paimon became a powerful Geo Slime and went to take revenge on the Forest Boar that used to bully Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But then the boar showed up with all its relatives, and Paimon lost again.

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: Wait, why did all of your dreams end so tragically?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Because Slimes are monsters, even though they look cute, they usually cause trouble and end up getting killed by adventurers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Things don't tend to end well for monsters. Believe Paimon.

choices.text: (I want to interrupt, but...)

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: I suppose you're right... They are monsters, after all.

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: I just want to experience a different life, but it seems that becoming a monster would be even worse than my current life.

response.speaker: Ata
response.text: Hmm, maybe I'd be happier if I became just a regular Finch or fish...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It looks like being an expert is way easier than Paimon imagined.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Next!

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Oh, it's my turn. Esteemed expert, I want to know what posture I should sleep in so I can have the same dream as the one I had last night.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, well...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes, please enlighten us, esteemed expert.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! You're supposed to be helping!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, first, why don't you tell Paimon about the dream you want to have again?

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Oh, it's quite ordinary. I sat and chatted with my wife on a sunny day, listening to the breeze blowing through the valley.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't you just find your wife and talk with her? There's no need to wait for a dream!

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Well, uh... Unfortunately, she passed away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh!? Uh, sorry! Paimon shouldn't have assumed anything.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: No, it's fine, I didn't make that clear. I just want a chance to see her again.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Have you tried looking at her photos right before you fall asleep?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it's not really about posture. What you think about right before falling asleep is probably way more important.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: Oh, is that all I have to do?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Think about it, if you're the one thinking about her, and you're the one that'll be dreaming about her, then it'll be easier to connect your thoughts and dreams.

response.speaker: Ilman
response.text: You do have a point... I'll give it a try tonight! Thanks for your wise advice!

response.speaker: Kathya
response.text: Oh, my turn, my turn! Ahem, I want to know the name of the plant in my dream!

response.speaker: Debbi
response.text: I want to bring the souvenir box in my room into my dream!

response.speaker: Pawlin
response.text: I dreamt of a raven flying over the wasteland last night. Does that have any kind of special meaning?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, no rush. One at a time!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After a long time, the "experts" finally conclude their work.

choices.text: (At least she's grasped the standard tropes of adventurer stories.)
Honestly, I don't have any good tips.

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: After talking so much about dreams, I'm feeling a little bit sleepy.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: I didn't expect the Dendro Archon to attend this event in person... It's like a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: What a lucky day... Just wait till my friends hear about this!

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: I wish my dreams could be a little more practical, you know... Maybe something like becoming rich and famous overnight.

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: It's just a dream. How bad could it be?

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: What's all the sudden commotion about?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...Another recurring dream?

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: Yeah, I'm starting to wonder if it's some kind of hint.

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: (I hope a lot of people will come to participate today.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you know what's the most important part of being an "expert"?

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: Ahem... Well, I suppose it must be accumulating knowledge and sharing your experiences?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nope, it's all about the title. From now on, Paimon will be known as "Paimon, the Dream Expert"!

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: O—Okay...

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: (If it IS a hint, well... I haven't seen them for a long time.)

dialogues.speaker: Pedrush
dialogues.text: (Should I continue expanding the scale of this event...?)

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: (Wow, it's really the Dendro Archon.)

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: ...(Or maybe a more exciting love life... Nah, who am I kidding...)

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: (The Dendro Archon made a really good point...)

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: (Maybe I should find a place to sleep, or go to the cafe...)

dialogues.speaker: Ilman
dialogues.text: (Haydar...)

dialogues.speaker: Debbi
dialogues.text: (Why am I so sleepy...?)

dialogues.speaker: Nasser
dialogues.text: (So some people are having pretty realistic dreams, big deal. What are they so worried about?)

dialogues.speaker: Pawlin
dialogues.text: (What happened? I need to ask someone and find out.)
